issues.legal_issue: The Central Empowered Committee may be institutionalised as a permanent statutory body under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, with its notification and continued functioning subject to the Supreme Court’s directions.
The Central Empowered Committee must adopt publicly accessible guidelines and procedures to ensure transparency, efficiency, and accountability in its functioning.

Environmental regulatory bodies must be institutionally structured and operated according to clear standards for composition, expertise, tenure, funding, mandates, coordination, transparency, public participation, accountability, and regular audits.
Constitutional courts have a continuing role in reviewing and monitoring the institutionalisation and functioning of environmental regulatory bodies to ensure environmental rule of law.
